title: Sinus rhythm
summary: Two leads of an ECG in sinus rhythm, with every beat labelled.
description: A minute of an ECG recorded on a portable recorder, in sinus rhythm: each beat starts with a P wave, followed by a QRS complex and a T wave, and the beats come at a fairly steady rate. The upper channel is a modified lead II, the lower one a chest lead (V5). Each beat was labelled by cardiologists (N: a normally conducted beat).
look_for: The P wave, the QRS complex and the T wave of each beat
The R–R interval between two beats, and the heart rate it gives (60 ÷ the R–R interval in seconds)
The PR interval (from the start of the P wave to the start of the QRS) and the QT interval (from the start of the QRS to the end of the T wave)

channels.name: ECG (lead II)
channels.about: a modified lead II: electrodes on the chest, near where those of lead II go on the limbs

channels.name: ECG (V5)
channels.about: a chest lead, over the left side of the heart

beats.note: Each beat was labelled by two cardiologists working independently, who then settled their differences (the reference labels of the MIT-BIH database).

legend.N: Normal beat: a normally conducted QRS (whatever the rhythm)

subject.notes: Taking Aldomet (methyldopa) and Inderal (propranolol), as the database records.
